HeldAsk.description:

its date, give it to another owner, send a question to someone else instead, drop it, or, for an ending of a
promise, move its date or record a part delivered; `ending`: the words said only that it is closed, so the person
is asked whether it is done by its owners or no longer needed), `item` the words of what it is about, `value` and
`from_value` the new and the present date, `to_name` the person it would go to, `told` the people a drop would

also carries what the input says happened: the action's id in `record`, its `owners` in the owner format,
`reporter` (who said it), and by ask the words of a new date (`due_words`) with the promise's own earlier words
(`earlier`), what was `delivered` and what is `left`, or the `reason` it is called off. The screen words the title
and the answers from these.

is work held until the person restarts the app (`count` waiting; the screen offers Restart now, which is
POST /api/restart); `paused` is an AI account waiting for its usage limit to reset (`account`, `until`, `count`
waiting), after which the work runs again by itself; `borrow` asks whether another kind of work's free account
(`account`, `model`) may take the `tier`'s work that waits on the paused account named in `text`, until `until`,
when that account's limit resets (`count` waiting items it would take, `estimate_usd`, `unpriced`; the answer is
POST /api/ai/borrow); `offline` is work that has waited for the network longer than
the configured time (`count` waiting, `waiting_since`), which runs again by itself once the network is back;
`catch_up_go` is the learning runs for the catch-up list held together for one go (`count`, `estimate_usd`,
`unpriced`; the go is POST /api/knowledge/catch-up/go); `intake_go` is a newly added source (`source`, `subject` its
label) whose first read is held for one go (`count` items, `estimate_usd` and `unpriced` for the total, `days` how
far back its mail was read, none for a source with no mail; the go is POST /api/watch/{source}/intake/go);
`intake_review` is what the first read of a newly added source found (`source`, `subject`, `count` items with
something to look over, `outcome` their results counted), one line in place of a line for each until the list is
opened (POST /api/watch/{source}/intake/seen); `credential` is a key or sign-in that stops working on
`due` or already has (`credential_kind`, `credential_name`, `waiting_days` left, below zero once past, and
`places`, everywhere the same credential is used); `switch_failed` is a switch of the `tier`'s account or model
whose check found problems or couldn't finish (the new `account`, the earlier one in `text`, `count` and `names`
of what didn't come out right, `check_failed` when it couldn't finish; Switch back is POST
/api/ai/switch/{tier}/back and Keep it POST /api/ai/switch/{tier}/keep); `account_move` is a saved account
(`account`, its service's name in `subject`) that uses the generic connection to a service that has its own (the
read-back is GET /api/ai/accounts/{account}/move, Move is POST to it and Not now POST .../move/not-now);
`model_watch` is news about an account's models (`account`, the tiers in `names`): with `state` newer, a newer model
of each tier's own family exists (`candidates`, by tier), `usd_per_day` what it would change in cost per day at
the current use (none when a price isn't known), `reason` why it isn't moved to on its own (asks, costs_more,
price_unknown, check_failed with `count` cases and `check_failed` when the check couldn't finish, or check_cost
with the check's `estimate_usd`); Switch is the settings' own switch with its check and Not now is POST
/api/ai/model-watch/{account}/{state}/not-now; with `state` price, a tier's current model went up in price by
`usd_per_day`; `model_moved` is a tier (`tier`) moved on its own to a newer model of its family after a check passed
(the new `account`, the earlier one in `text`, `usd_per_day` the change in cost; Switch back and Keep are the
switch routes above); `identity` is a command-line agent
account (`account`) whose sign-in changed (`state` changed: the sign-in found now in `text`, the recorded one in
`subject`; Keep is POST /api/ai/accounts/{account}/identity/keep, Sign in again opens the account) or isn't set
for the level of the work waiting on it (`state` level: `text` the sign-in, none when unknown, `names` the levels
of the waiting work, `count` the requests); `work_access` is an account (`account`) the person answered "Not now"
about reading their work mail and notes (Allow is POST /api/ai/accounts/{account}/allow-work, with Undo, and the
line goes once the account may see the internal level); `no_account` is work with no AI account
at all (`count` kinds of work, their tiers in `names`, the first in `tier`); `extractor` is a kind of file that
isn't being read (`file_kind`, and `text` says why), which clears once a file of that kind reads well;
`source_unread` is a watched source that has failed for longer than its usual gap (`source` its id, `subject` its
label, `problem_kind` the kind of failure, `text` what went wrong and what to do, `waiting_since` when it was last
read, or first tried when it never was), which clears once it is read again; `promise` is one open action that
needs a look: the person's own past its date, or one someone else owes with its date near or past, or with none and
nothing heard for a while (its id in `actions`, its words in `text` and `subject`, its day in `due`, none when it is
undated, `waiting_days` past that day, below zero while it is ahead, or days with nothing heard when undated, and
`person`, the one to chase, none when it is the person's own; its choices are the action's own routes and GET
/api/promises/{id} says why it exists); `reminder` is an open action whose reminder has reached the person (its id
in `actions`, its words in `text` and `subject`, `at` the moment it was set for, `late` when it came due while the
app or the computer was not running, and `snoozes` the choices that still have a time, each with the moment it
moves the reminder to; a snooze is POST /api/reminders/{id}); `reminder_digest` is the reminders that waited, shown
together: those that fell in quiet hours (`late` false) or, when the person chose one summary, those missed while
the computer slept (`late` true), each in `reminders`; `reply` is a reply the person owes, one open action (its id
in `actions`, its words in `text`, the message's `subject`, who it is to in `person` or, for nobody known, `sender`
as written, and the drafted `reply` with `reply_reviewed`; Copy reply and Edit are POST /api/actions/{id}/reply, No
reply needed is POST /api/actions/{id}/drop and Answered another way is POST /api/replies/{id}/answered, each with
Undo); `sent_check` asks whether a message the person copied went out (`sent_copy` its copy's id, `person` who it
was for, `questions` and `actions` what it covered; the answers are POST /api/copies/{id}/settle with `how`,
each undone by POST /api/copies/{id}/unsettle; it is there only while a sent folder is being read and no sent
message has matched the copy); `since_yesterday` is what the assistant or a rule did that the person hasn't looked
over, one line for all of it (`count` entries, counted by act in `outcome`; Look over opens GET
/api/since-yesterday, and opening it is POST /api/since-yesterday/seen);
`away` is one row for the lines that waited for the person's working hours (or
for quiet hours to end) and arrived together with them (`count` of them; it has no choices and goes with the day);
`escalate` suggests asking someone else about one thing (`text` its words, in `questions` or `actions` its id,
`person` who hasn't answered, `count` the follow-ups it has had, `waiting_days` the days since the last word; Pick
who is POST /api/questions/{id}/reroute for a question and POST /api/records/edit on the action's owners for an
action, each with Undo; nothing is ever sent); `stale` is the person's own open to-dos nobody has touched for
`ui.today.stale_after_days` (`count` of them, their ids in `actions`, `waiting_days` the oldest's days untouched;
Look over opens GET /api/open-items narrowed to them); `unfiled` is
what the assistant filed under no project (`count` items, never zero: with none there is no line; they are listed
by GET /api/unfiled; `state` which_side when a business is set, so the line is the one question of which side
they belong to, the business's name in `subject`); `nudge` is the one follow-up line for a person the person is
waiting on (`person`, `count` their items, `overdue` how many are past their date with the oldest in `due`,
`waiting_days` the longest wait; it opens the one message to them, GET /api/followups); `backup` is no backup
that works (`state`, and `age_hours` since the last one that did; Back up now is POST /api/backup).

check_failed.description: For an account_check line: true when the account's last check failed, false when it was never checked for that work. For a switch_failed line: true when the check couldn't finish.

credential_kind.description: For a credential line: an AI account's key or an add-on's sign-in.

credential_name.description: For a credential line: the account's short name or the sign-in's name.
credential_name.title: Credential Name

deciding.description: For a review line: the keys of the lines under Decide that ask about its own held ops, which the line leaves out of its count and the screen links to.

did.description: For a review line that covers one applied op: what it did, as the op's name and the item's own words, which the screen says in the past tense; null when the line groups several.

estimate_usd.description: The estimated cost of everything the line starts (first_go, catch_up_go, intake_go), when any has a price.

expired.description: For a learned line: how many proposals from inputs expired unreviewed since the person last looked at what was learned.

file_kind.description: For an extractor line: the kind of file that isn't being read (document, spreadsheet, presentation, pdf or text), or the label an add-on gave its own kind. `text` says why.
file_kind.title: File Kind

held.description: For a held line that rests on an inference or would drop something that reached someone: the question it asks. Keeping things as they are is POST /api/changesets/{id}/ops/{index}/decline.

key.description: Stable while the thing it stands for waits.
key.title: Key

late.description: For a reminder line: true when it came due and was not shown in time. For a reminder_digest line: true when it lists reminders that were missed, false when it lists those that waited for quiet hours to end.

left_out.description: For a catch_up line: how many kinds of earlier correction were too many for the list and expired unread.

model.description: For an account_check line: the short name of the account's model in that chain.

moved.description: For a rule_review line: how many rules the latest run had moved out of the always-sent part, so they go only to the runs they cover.

names.description: For a switch_failed line: what the check found didn't come out right, by name, the first few.

notes.description: For a line about one action: that action's notes, which the screen shows on hover and in the inspector.

op.description: The held item's index in its changeset.

origins.description: For a learned line: how many of the proposals came from an input (`input`) and how many from one of the person's corrections (`correction`).
origins.title: Origins

overdue.description: For a nudge line: how many of its items are past their date; `due` is the oldest of those.

parent_name.description: The name of the project its project is part of, if any.

person.description: Whom the line is about (send, nudge).

places.description: For a credential line: every place the same credential is used, in plain words.

problem_kind.description: For a source_unread line: the kind of failure (auth, no_access, not_found, outage, or another kind a connector reports), which the screen words as what to do.

reason.description: For a model_watch line of a newer model: why it isn't moved to on its own (asks, costs_more, price_unknown, check_failed or check_cost).

reminders.description: For a reminder_digest line: the reminders it lists, oldest first.

replies.description: For a promise or nudge line: how many replies that didn't answer its promise has had since the line began (the most of its promises, for a nudge). The line says it: "replied twice without a date".

reply.description: For a reply line: the reply the assistant drafted, none when no recorded fact holds the answer.

rules.description: For a rule_review line: the ids of the rules flagged, most present first.

sender.description: For a reply line to nobody known: who the message is from, as the message writes it.

sent_copy.description: For a sent_check line: the id of the copy the person is asked about.

snoozes.description: For a reminder line: the snooze choices that still have a time, in order, each with the moment it resolves to. A choice with no time left today is not listed.
snoozes.title: Snoozes

source.description: For a source_unread line: the watched source's id; its label is in GET /api/watch.

stable_budget.description: For a rule_review line: the size that section may be before rules move out of it.
stable_budget.title: Stable Budget

stable_size.description: For a rule_review line: the size of what every run is sent, in characters, on the latest run.
stable_size.title: Stable Size

stance.description: For a promise line someone else owes: who they are to the person (design 6.34). The screen says Chase for manage and alongside, and Waiting on, with no follow-up, for report_to; null for the person's own.
stance.title: Stance

state.description: For a model_watch line: newer (a newer model of a tier's family exists) or price (a tier's current model went up in price). For a handover line: diverged (this computer and the synced folder each changed; the person chooses which copy to keep), chosen (the choice waits for the restart) or elsewhere (another computer opened the workspace, so this copy stopped writing to the folder). `text` is the other computer's name. For an identity line: changed (the agent's sign-in is a different one than the one recorded) or level (its sign-in isn't set for the level of the work waiting). For a backup line: unset (no backup folder is chosen), never (a folder, and no backup has worked yet), failed (the last try failed and none has worked) or overdue (the last one that worked is older than it should be; `age_hours` says how old). For an unfiled line: which_side when a business is set, so the line asks which side the items belong to, once, for all of them.

subject.description: The one thing's own words when a review or overdue line covers exactly one, which the screen uses as the line's title; null when the line groups several.
subject.title: Subject

suggestion.description: For an owner line: who the routing entries suggest owns the action and why, and the nearest open action to fold it into; none when nothing applies.

text.description: The decision, question, name or held item in one line.
text.title: Text

tier.description: For an account_check line: the tier whose fallback chain holds the account. For a switch_failed line: the tier that was switched.
tier.title: Tier

title.description: The input the line is about.

unpriced.description: How many of the things the line starts have no price (first_go, catch_up_go, intake_go).
unpriced.title: Unpriced

until.description: When the account's limit resets and the work waiting on it runs again by itself (paused), or when the line comes back if the person says Not now (rule_review), on the person's own clock (their time zone).
until.title: Until

usd_per_day.description: For a model_watch or model_moved line: what the change costs per day at the current use, in US dollars (below zero: less); none when a price isn't known.
usd_per_day.title: Usd Per Day

waiting.description: Why the work stopped, in plain words.
waiting.title: Waiting

waiting_since.description: When the oldest request waiting for the network began waiting (offline), on the person's own clock (their time zone).
waiting_since.title: Waiting Since

post.description:
Drop an action that is no longer needed, with a reason and Undo. It is never done or credited, and it leaves
every list. Records a dropped correction naming the change and run that made it, when there was one.
Ask the assistant to draft the work an open action stands for. The action stays the person's.
Put an open action on hold, waiting for something. It is never due, overdue or chased while it is.
Undo a put on hold or a take off hold: the hold goes back to what it was, and no signal is recorded.

Keep this action and close the one it nearly repeats, as one change with one Undo. Its notes gain the other's
words, it takes the earlier date, and the other is dropped, which is a correction the assistant learns from.

Make an open to-do repeat as the words say, with Undo. A to-do with no day is due on the first day the words
fall on; words that aren't clear, or a day that isn't one of theirs, are refused in plain words.
Stop an open to-do repeating, with Undo. It stays as it is; no next one is made when it ends.
Take an action off hold; it is due again by its own due date.

Keep the draft made for an action exactly as the person copied it (the draft waiting for review, else the
text they approved), so the message they then send can be matched to it. The action stays open: copying is not
doing. Copying it again moves the same copy forward.

get.description:
The acts, newest first; with `status` (repeat it for several), only those in one of those states (Waiting to
go out reads draft, approved, stale, failed and uncertain), and with `limit`, at most that many.
One act: its exact content and target, the fingerprint a yes would cover and the recipients called out.

post.description:
The person's yes on this exact act: the fingerprint their screen showed and the recipients called out they
acknowledged. Nothing is sent. A different fingerprint, or a recipient not acknowledged, is refused.

Approve and send in one, after the yes. An act already approved is sent as it stands, and only when the
fingerprint named is the one the yes covers. The publisher checks again at send time.

The person's answer for an act the app can't confirm went out (or one they carried out themselves): `sent`
marks it sent; `again` approves it again as it is and sends it, or, when what the yes covered changed, makes it
stale and needs a new yes. Undo takes `sent` back.

Take back a sent act where its channel can (a mailbox act, an event it created): the person's request is
recorded as theirs, then the channel is asked once. A refusal or no answer leaves the act sent, with the reason
on it. A sent message, or a change or answer others were told of, is refused.
Take an act back: it will not go. Undo brings it back as it was.

Give one secret an add-on declares, with Undo: typed (kept on this computer, a local app only) or as
where it is kept. The settings hold only where.

Check a new account before it is saved, the moment its key is pasted: every kind of work is tried with the
exact settings it will use, and the answer says in words that fit the kind of account what to do when it fails.
Nothing is kept: the key is used for this request only.

get.description: The AI accounts in the settings, as they are on disk now; never a key.

schema.title: Response Ai Accounts Api Ai Accounts Get

post.description:
Give an account a new key, other models or other work, with Undo. A switch of a tier's account or model
made this way is made at once, without the check.

The person's yes to an account reading their work mail and notes: it may see the internal level (and
keeps any level above it), and Today stops asking. One settings change, so Undo puts the answer back.

Keep the sign-in an agent account now runs as: it is recorded in place of the earlier one, the line on Today
goes, and the work that waited on it tries again.

get.description:
Which identity the account's service's own connection would sign in as: its key (its last four characters,
and whether it is the one in use now), its address and its name. Nothing is called or changed.

post.description:
Move the account to its service's own connection, on the person's yes: the account check (one call per tier
and kind of work with its exact parameters) runs on the new connection first, and only a check that passed
writes the change, through the settings save, with Undo. A failed check leaves the account as it was.
Put the move off for good: its line on Today never comes back unasked.

Remove an account, with Undo. The work it did goes to the backup named in `take_over` (the backup's own entry
for that kind of work becomes its main one), or, with none named, has no account until one is chosen. Its kept
key stays on this computer, so Undo brings the account back whole.

Make the change and check it: when it switches a tier's account or model, the golden cases and the add-ons'
own cases run on the new choice in the background, and a failure comes to Today with Switch back.

What the check that comes with this change would cost, and whether one is offered: only a change that
switches a tier's account or model, while checks on a switch are on. Nothing is saved.

Test one account, whether or not any kind of work uses it yet: on the model named, else its first. With a
tier, the test uses that tier's kinds of work and their exact parameters, which is what lets the account be
added to that tier's fallbacks.

schema.title: Response Ai Account Test Api Ai Accounts  Name  Test Post

post.description:
Answer the question of using another kind of work's account until the paused account's limit resets. A yes
lets the waiting work run on that account at once and lasts until the reset; a no keeps it waiting.

get.description:
What one account's connection check involves (calls and tokens), so a screen can price it with the price of
the model the person picks.

schema.title: Response Endpoints Api Ai Endpoints Get

get.description: Model servers running on this computer now, with their models; none on a hosted app.

schema.title: Response Ai Local Api Ai Local Get

post.description:
Put off what a line about an account's models says (`state` newer or price), until a different newer model
or a different price rise appears.
The models a service offers, read with a key that isn't saved, so the person picks from a list.

get.description:
Which model does what (design 7.9): each kind of work (the core's and every running add-on's) with the tier
it uses now, what was measured for the model each tier uses, the cheapest tier that passed, each tier with its
account and second try, the routing rules in the order they are checked, and the rules the measurements back.

What each account's models can do, from the evaluation runs kept in this workspace: per model and skill the
pass rate, the runs, the age of the last one, the cost of a passing run and whether it is stale or under the
minimum score (design 6.16). A skill nobody measured is listed as not measured.

post.description:
What measuring this account would cost: its models (or the one named) on the golden cases, the add-ons'
cases and the learning pairs, only those whose material the account is allowed to see, each as many times as
the configured number of runs. Nothing is run or spent.

Measure this account in the background, filling what it can do (`GET /api/ai/skills`). A cost above the
amount the person asked to be asked about is refused unless `confirmed` is sent; an account that may see none
of the cases has nothing to measure.

Put a tier back as it was before the switch whose check didn't pass, or before a move made on its own, with
Undo.
Keep a switch whose check didn't pass, or a move made on its own: the line goes.

get.description: Where the key that encrypts the backups is read from; never the key.

post.description:
Give the key that encrypts the backups, with Undo: typed, made by the app, or as where it is kept. A local
app keeps a typed or made key on this computer. Backups already made stay sealed with the key they were made
with, so an earlier key is kept, not replaced.
Add a meeting, or merge it into the one that is already on the calendar. The person's own act, with Undo.

Keep things as they are for a held item: it isn't applied and leaves the list, and the choice is a
correction the assistant learns from.

Answer "Done by <owner>, or no longer needed?" for an ending whose words only said it was closed: done
credits the owners, no longer needed credits nobody. Either applies at once, with Undo.

Add an action waiting for an owner to the open action it nearly repeats, as one change with Undo. The
waiting action closes as dropped, its words are kept in the other action's notes, and a declined correction is
recorded naming the action it went into.

A project the assistant found isn't one: the proposal is set aside and the words are kept as a glossary
entry saying so, as one change with Undo. Records a declined correction.

A project the assistant found is part of an existing one: the work of that change goes under it, the words
are kept as a glossary entry naming it, and the proposal is set aside, as one change with Undo. Records a
declined correction.
Take back keeping a held item as it was: it waits for the person again.
The person's answer to whether a message they copied went out. Returns what Undo takes.
Undo an answer: the copy is asked about again as before, and a Not sent is marked as sent again.

get.description: The kinds of data file running add-ons let the person edit through a form.

schema.title: Response Forms Api Data Forms Get

get.description:
One file as a form: its fields (from the schema) with the values in effect, and the layer they come from;
a file that doesn't exist yet shows the schema's defaults.

post.description: Save the workspace's or a project's copy with these changes, checked against the schema; `before` undoes.

schema.title: Response Files Api Data Forms  Name  Files Get

post.description: Remove the workspace's or a project's copy; the less specific one is in effect again.
Undo a save or a removal: the layer's copy as it was before.

Make the to-do a plain calendar entry is offered as (its title starts with a task verb), as the person's own
change: owned by them, due on the entry's day and moving with it. Undo takes the changeset.

get.description:
The failures of the last `ui.feedback_problem_days` days, newest first and at most `ui.feedback_problem_max`:
failed AI calls, account checks and source reads, and errors in the app. Each has when, what was being done,
the account's service, adapter and program version, the request's settings, the status, the error kind and the
service's own error text. Secrets, addresses, paths and the names of the workspace's own people, projects and
files are masked; nothing the person wrote or read is in it. The app sends nothing: the person sends it.

schema.title: Response File Kinds Api File Kinds Get

post.description:
Add a file: the request body is the file's bytes, its Content-Type the media type, details as JSON. Without
a `data_level` the file takes its kind's level (internal unless the kind says otherwise).

get.description: A file's bytes. Images may show in the app; everything else downloads; nothing is rendered as a page.

post.description:
Close an action because the person it waits on finished it: credited to them, reported by the PM. A note
typed with it goes to the assistant.

Record that the PM chased a person about an open action: it stays open and counts as told again. A note
typed with it goes to the assistant.

Record that the follow-up message went to a person: each question and action it listed counts as chased
today, and the wait for an answer starts again.

Hold a person's whole message for a meeting, a series or a day: every question in it that is ready to send
waits in Later, in one change, and comes back numbered as before. Undo posts `previous` to the restore route.
Undo a held message: each question goes back to what it was held for.
Undo a follow-up marked as sent.

"Change this" on a row the assistant made: an action, question, decision, calendar entry (kind `event`)
or fact. Records a correction and queues the assistant's work on the note; the packet carries the item as it
is now.

get.description: Plugins' scheduled work: whether it runs, how often, and how its last run went.
What the assistant learned, newest first, with where each piece came from; filter by kind and by status.

What the assistant learned from corrections made before it could learn from them: one list, the most
repeated kinds of correction first, cut at the configured number.

post.description:
The person's go for the learning runs held for the catch-up list: every one starts, and the list fills as
they finish.

get.description:
What the assistant is learning or has learned from each correction that has something to show, for the line
under that correction's card: still being learned (with why it waits), a proposal to keep, or the person's own
words already kept, with the change that undoes them. What the catch-up list holds is left out.

What the assistant learned that waits for the person, oldest first, each tagged by where it came from
(an input or one of the person's corrections) with its evidence and what it applies to. The catch-up list is
separate.

The standing rules, newest first, each with where it came from, what it applies to and constrains, and how
much the runs used it; filter by status.

schema.title: Response Rules Api Knowledge Rules Get

get.description:
The standing rules to look over: active rules given to runs over the review window and never shown to apply,
most present first, with the size of what every run is sent and how many rules the latest run had moved out of
it. A rule a code check enforces is never in the list.

post.description:
"Not now" on the rules review line: the line leaves Today for `knowledge.rule_review_every_days`, as it does
when the person keeps, narrows or retires a rule, so the person never has to decide something to make it go
away. It records a `not_now` signal naming the rules flagged, and changes no rule.
Undo "Not now": the line is back on Today at once.
Discard a proposed entry. It is kept, with the reason if one is given. Undo puts it back to proposed.

Set a proposal aside as right for this case but not a pattern: it is discarded with that as its reason,
a `just_this_time` signal is recorded, and the same correction proposed again is shown with how many times
this was said before. Undo puts it back to proposed.

Keep a proposed entry: it becomes active, and the person is its author, with the wording or target they
changed here. Undo puts it back to proposed.

Keep a standing rule as it is in the review: the clock for its next review starts now. Undo puts the old
clock back.

Narrow what an active rule or entry applies to. It is the person's own change of its scope, so Undo puts the
old scope back.

Retire an active entry or standing rule: it stops guiding runs and stays on record, with the same `retired`
signal for both. Undo makes it active again.

get.description: The tone, and for a status list the meaning, offered for a value being added; the person can change both.
Every value list, with the fields that use it.

schema.title: Response Value Lists Api Lists Get

post.description: Add a value to a list (or offer a retired one again), with Undo.

Merge one value of a list into another: records that hold the first hold the second, and the first leaves
the list. With Undo.
Rename a value on a list and on every record that holds it, with Undo.
Stop offering a value; records that hold it keep it. Undo offers it again.

Move a mail item to the Set aside folder, as personal or sales mail, and close its request if one is
waiting for the assistant.
Name the person the app is for: renames their person record, or makes one and links it in the settings.

"Missed one" (design 6.32): the person says in a plain sentence what the assistant missed. Records a missed
correction for them and hands the words in as their own note, marked as a miss, so the run adds what was
missed. The request's own changes have their own Undo.

get.description: Every filed note, newest first, with the project it was filed under (if any).
What the notices are set to now, and why the last note to the address didn't arrive when it didn't.

post.description:
"Send me a test": the webhook gets the test note now (even with notices off, so it can be checked first);
for the browser the answer carries the words, which the open screen shows itself.

get.description: What the open screen shows a browser notice for. Empty while notices or the browser target are off.

post.description:
Give the person's own address for notices, with Undo: typed (kept on this computer, a local app only) or as
where it is kept. The settings hold only where; the address is never sent back.

get.description:
Every action still to do, with its owners, due date, project, parent project and where it came from, and
every
question still waiting, with who it waits on and since when.
The organizations people work for, by name.

post.description: Rename or change an organization. People refer to it by id, so a new name shows everywhere at once.
List another catalog of add-ons, by its address, with Undo. It is read when the screen asks to refresh.
Take a catalog the person listed off the list, with Undo. The add-ons already installed stay.

Turn an add-on off, with Undo: it stops after the restart the person chooses; its records and settings
stay.

Turn on an add-on installed on this computer: it is added to the add-ons that run, with Undo. Its code
runs after the restart the person chooses.

Install (or update) an add-on from the release file its catalog entry names, checked against the entry's
checksum. It isn't turned on; it is used after the restart the person chooses.

Give the read token for the place an add-on's release file is kept, with Undo. A local app keeps a typed
token in its private folder and the settings hold only where; the token is sent only to that place.
Remove an add-on installed from this screen. Its records and settings stay; turn it off first.

get.description: The screens running plugins add; with a project, only those its add-on lists on that project.
A document panel's blocks for the project in view, or the workspace.

What the assistant knows about a project: where its inputs come from and the last of each, its facts with
who they rest on and when, the glossary terms used there, who answers what, and what is still unknown with the
question asked for it.

Why a promise exists and what is known of it: its words, who owes it to whom, its day and the words it came
from, where it came from, how it is known, and what was heard since.

post.description:
Correct who owes a promise, to whom, how it is known or its day, with Undo. Records an edited correction
for what the assistant had set.

get.description:
The knowledge-used rate for each kind of work, the repeat-correction rate for each kind of work and week
(only weeks with enough corrections have a rate), and the weekly list of what runs said no op could do,
grouped by wording with counts, "Missed one" for each person and week (design 6.32), and missed, declined and
dropped each counted on its own (a drop is not a correction of the assistant), over the configured window;
and the gate week's instruments, each a count with its denominator for each day and for the window: silent
closes out of all closes, wrong endings out of endings made, the person's own missed out of present,
and the replay set.

put.description:
Save the person's own count for a day, or correct it: how many promises they counted on their own list
(`present`) and how many of those the app didn't have (`missed`). Returns what the day held before, which
Undo takes.

post.description: Undo a save: the day holds what it held before, or nothing.

get.description: The questions closed as dropped, newest first, with the reason the person gave.

schema.title: Response Dropped Api Questions Dropped Get

post.description:
Answer a question to the PM. A question asking who (who a name is, who owns an action) takes a person and
lets the item it holds go ahead; any other question takes a written answer.
Drop a question with a reason, with Undo. It stays on record, listed at GET /api/questions/dropped.

get.description:
What "Add a new person" starts with for a "Who is this?" question: the name as written and what the input
says about them.

post.description:
Answer a "Who is this?" question with a new person, saved as the person's own with Undo. An organization no
record has is added with them, the held items waiting on the name go ahead, and a routed correction is
recorded naming the new person. Undo the released items first, then the changes in `undo`.
Hand in a person's reply to a question that went out, with a note saying which question it answers.

Ask someone else instead, with Undo. Records a routed correction; a decision stays a decision for the new
person.
Reword a question, with Undo. Records a reworded correction.
Record that the person already sent this question themselves, with Undo.

Hold an unsent question for a meeting, a series or a day (it waits in Later, out of To send, until that
day), or send it now (no hold). Undo puts back what `previous` says.

get.description: Any record's page: core or a plugin's, by its kind.

post.description: The person's own change to fields of a shown record, with Undo.

schema.title: Response Record Stage History Api Records  Record Id  Stage History Get

Set an action's reminder to a snooze choice or to a time the person picked, with Undo; with neither, clear
it. A time that has passed, or a choice with no time left, is refused in plain words.
What the words typed for a repeat are read as, from the to-do's day (or today). Nothing is kept.

Close a reply owed because it was answered another way (a call, a chat), credited to the person, with their
words as the evidence when they give any, and Undo. It is the person's own act, so it teaches nothing.

Keep the drafted reply of a reply owed exactly as the person copied it, so the message they then send can be
matched to it. Copying it again moves the same copy forward.

get.description: The accounts that may take this request's material, for sending it somewhere else after a refusal.

post.description:
Let the account that would take a stopped request see its material's level, at once and with Undo, then
queue the request again. Only a request stopped because no account may see its level.
Hand in a change a triage rule closed after all; the correction is kept so rules can be tuned.
Restart now, because the person chose to (never on its own). It starts between pieces of work.

get.description:
What the first go's sorting run would add to the estimate of the runs waiting for it, so the person approves
the whole spend. Nothing when no run waits for the go or no mail needs sorting.

post.description:
The person's first go: the mail handed in unsorted while it was pending is sorted first (the go covers that
run), then every run still waiting for it starts, and no run waits for it again.

get.description: What the UI needs before anything else: where it is served, what to call things, and its settings.

A series' page: the next meeting with what is open for it by person (the person last), and the meetings
that passed, each with what was settled and what moved on.
The Set aside folder: mail kept away from the assistant, in two sections, newest first.

post.description:
Confirm set-aside mail was rightly set aside: a sender rule is written for each distinct sender, and the
messages leave the folder and are deleted from the app after their undo time.
Undo a confirmation within its undo time: the messages are back in the folder.
Undo a set-aside the person made by hand: the message and its request go back as they were.
This is work: hand the message in after all, as Take a closer look does, and keep the correction.
Leave every add-on that is off now off: the setup step counts as done until another is installed.

Back up to a cloud drive found on this computer: its backup folder is made, saved as a target, and the first
backup is made before the answer, so the reminder to back up is gone when the person goes on.

get.description:
The cloud drives found on this computer, by name, for the backup step: the first is recommended. None when
the app isn't on the person's own computer, which has no drive folders to look at.

Whether the person has a business and what it is called, for the Personal / business filter. A business whose
project was undone or removed counts as none.

post.description:
Say what the person's business is called: makes its top-level project and sets `project.business`; saying it
again renames that project. With Undo.

get.description:
Where the first result stands: the look back offered with its estimate, under way, or done with the
promises found and one follow-up ready. Writes nothing.

post.description: The person's go for the look back: everything it counted starts, as the go on Today's line does.
Keep where the walkthrough stands: its screen, that it was closed, or that it was finished.

delete.description:
Sign out of a service: one account, by its key (`?account=`), or every account when none is named. Only the
sources reading with a signed-out account stop, with the usual line asking to sign in again.

reads with that connector yet: one click instead of filling in a source by hand.

(the person turned acting on for the account); without it, reading only.

The closes nobody has seen (a rule's, the set-aside sorting's, the assistant's own drops and closes) in the
configured quality window, newest first, and the measure: silent closes out of all closes.

The person saw a close and it stands. A rule's close is marked as seen; the assistant's is approved by
looking over its change. Mail set aside is confirmed in its folder instead.

What the assistant or a rule did since the start of yesterday (or the last time the list was opened, when
that is later), newest first, one entry for each record.

post.description:
The person opened the list as it was drawn at `until`: everything made up to then counts as seen, and Today's
line goes until something new happens.
The person widens who may see a limited message, or removes the limit, with Undo.

same checks the command line has; nothing about the workspace changes until then.

Plugin AI work the person can start on a record of `kind` (or on the workspace with no kind); with `id`,
only the work offered on that record.

stops the others; its problem shows on the source as after any read.

then waiting on the person, due within the follow-up window, then at risk; one line for each other person; a
blocked action only as the question or action that holds it up; the blocked counted; and the dated to-dos of

the meetings to hold, across projects.

newest first.

File several items under one project as the person's own edit, in one change with Undo. Each item's

its settings take. Kinds made only for tests are left out.

post.description:
Always set aside mail from these senders and domains as personal or sales, or never set it aside, as the
person's own rule, with Undo. Keeping mail goes first in the list; the rule applies to the next mail.
Start reading a new source, with Undo. Its id comes from its label.
Change a source's name, how often it is read, whether it is read, or its settings, with Undo.
Stop reading a source and take it off the list, with Undo; what it already handed in stays.

The folders of a mailbox source, and which the server marks as sent mail, for offering the sent folder as a
source of its own. Reads the mailbox; nothing there changes.

held for the go starts.

still need a look. Undo is POST /api/watch/{source_id}/intake/unseen.
Undo marking the intake seen: the results are one line on Today again.

mail that far back. Writes nothing.

Look further back: the older mail the source already returned is taken in the same quiet way as its first
read, under the same go rules, and the day it was looked back to moves.

Hand the assistant what the source holds from the recent past or near future that it hasn't seen yet (the
last day's mail, today's meetings), after a first read that only noted what was there.

Read a mailbox's sent folder as a source of its own, with Undo: the same mailbox, the same sign-in, the
folder picked from its list, and the person as its author, since what is in it is their own mail. It is taken in
quietly like any new source.
